cover_note: Hi Victor. I rebuilt UniiChat from revision 3c190e06 of your specification, as closely as the Claude Code CLI allows, and ran it on a subscription beside a plain continued session; that comparison is mine, not one your text makes. My test chat was short (60 logged messages, 21.7 KB, never near the 128 KB batch), so it says nothing about the regime the design is for, and the parts I could exercise behaved as you describe. The one result I think carries to a long chat is compaction work: Haiku at xhigh took a median of 6,165 output tokens for a leaf and 13,037 for a merge, almost all of it thinking, and merges were 81% of the total. Is that what you see, and would a lower effort with more retries do, given that I got 96% first-try fit at xhigh against 59% at default? I would also like to know how you run it (API billing or subscription, which model for turns), roughly how many messages it takes you to reach the first batch, and whether you have seen a standing order, as opposed to a correction, drop out of the view. The write-up lists every place my harness departs from your design: [link]. A 250-turn tool-heavy run at your real limits is next, so tell me if there is something you would want measured in it.
